verdict.rationale: Jitsu Functions are documented as running in-pipeline before data reaches destinations, with explicit filter, transform and enrich modes. They are written in JavaScript/TypeScript and add a Fetch API, Warehouse API, persistent storage and logging, plus a debugger and a CLI that scaffolds, tests and deploys them. One HN launch-era comment said a Segment Functions equivalent 'doesn't seem present', but that is an impression rather than a concrete hands-on failure, so it lowers confidence without creating a dispute. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that Functions work as documented in production.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can transform, filter, and enrich events in-pipeline with custom code or functions before they reach destinations

citations.quote: Filter - Exclude data that fails to meet your specified criteria. Transform - Modify data to fit the schema of your destination. Enrich - Add extra information to the event.
Functions are designed to process data in Jitsu before it is sent to the destination. These functions, written in JavaScript, provide various data handling options
Filter, transform, and enrich events with TypeScript functions before they land.
Fetch API - Perform HTTP requests to third-party services. Warehouse API - Query your data warehouses.
`jitsu-cli init` scaffolds a TypeScript project with tests, and `jitsu-cli deploy` ships it to your workspace.
